text:
For a period and a bit, the Oilers had the afternoon they wanted in Raleigh. Owen Michaels scored on a 5% chance, Leon Draisaitl buried a power-play goal off Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard, and Mathieu Joseph added a shorthanded goal early in the second for a 3-1 lead. Then Carolina simply took the game away, scoring six of the last eight goals and winning 7-4.

The comeback started with the unlikeliest goals of the day. Sean Walker scored on a chance worth under 1%, and Jalen Chatfield did the same, with Jordan Staal, freshly back from injured reserve, picking up an assist. Taylor Hall, the first overall pick the Oilers made in 2010, tied it 3-3 on a backhand at 11:51 of the second, a goal that moved Carolina's win chance from 31% to 52%. Andrei Svechnikov put the Hurricanes ahead on the power play 43 seconds later. Vasily Podkolzin answered on the power play, but Sebastian Aho scored with 26 seconds left in the period, another power-play goal, and Carolina never trailed again. Svechnikov's slapper in the third and Alexander Nikishin's late power-play goal finished it.

The scoreboard was tight for a while; the ice never was. Carolina had 74 shot attempts to 33, 36 shots to 15, and 3.68 expected goals (the quality of the chances) to 1.50. Replay every shot and the Hurricanes win 84% of the time. They owned the third period 1.83 to 0.32. Svechnikov, with two goals, added the most wins of anyone, and Aho had a goal and two assists. The defending champions look like themselves.

The hard afternoon belonged to Devon Levi, who had been the story in Edmonton, setting an Oilers record with 10 wins in 11 games. He allowed seven on 36 shots, 3.3 more than they deserved, though he also made the best save of the game on Logan Stankoven early. Pyotr Kochetkov allowed four on 15 shots at the other end, which mattered less than it might have. Edmonton won the first meeting in a shootout in October; this one was never that close in the run of play.
headline: Carolina erases a two-goal hole and buries Edmonton
